text:
mina: RFC follow-up: propose a sparse-serializer + micro-backstop image for on‑prem delta upgrades. goal: safe partial-replay, resumable apply, and deterministic rollback across reboots.

raj: why sparse-serializer vs compatibility shim in agent?

mina: sparse-serializer is an encoding label. deltas include serializer=v1 or v2. controller routes only to agents that advertise the serializer via `GET /capabilities`. avoids growing agent runtime with shims. fallback path: if agent lacks serializer, controller triggers backstop pull or full-image swap.

sam: full-image swap is heavy. how big is backstop and how does operator trigger it?

mina: backstop is ~120MB gz (verifier + replay engine + health probe). controller can call `POST /pull-backstop?manifest=<sha256>` so operators can prefetch before apply. backstop only needs to validate headers and stream chunks into blobstore.

elaine: capability contract suggestion: `GET /capabilities` -> {"serializers":["v1","v2"],"apply_modes":["swap","stream"]}. `POST /delta` accepts header `X-Serializer: v2`.

jules: include a compatibility matrix in the console and release notes listing clusters needing the backstop. ops will want a timeline.

raj: tradeoff: per-chunk sha256 increases manifest size ~8-12% but enables resumable partial apply and safe GC of staged blobs. prefer checksummed chunks.

mina: propose manifest-v3 minimal fields: serializer, manifest_version=3, chunks=[{sha256,size}], backstop_uri, apply_mode=(swap|stream), signer_key_id. keep simple to ease agent parsers.

sam: stream vs swap: stream writes directly and uses less disk, but abort/rollback is tricky. swap writes to tmp and atomically renames; safer but higher disk use.

elaine: default to swap unless operator explicitly sets stream for constrained devices. console should surface preflight checks.

ops-bot: rollout-scan: staging report: 4/30 nodes v1-only; these will use backstop or swap fallback.

nikhil: add `/healthz?manifest=<sha256>` on backstop image to verify manifest header and basic chunk availability without applying. installers can assert integrity after pull.

mina: action items: (1) spec `/capabilities` + `X-Serializer` header (2) implement manifest-v3 encoder in packager (3) build backstop image with `/healthz` and publish artifact manifest (4) console UX: rollout modal shows compatibility window and missing-capability graph.

raj: compatibility policy: mixed-cluster support for 14 days after release. after that, new deltas requiring v2 will be blocked; console warns cluster owners. call it out in release notes and enterprise docs.

jules: add an automated scan that emails cluster owners when they fall behind, include redwoodctl snips.

sam: CLI examples for docs: `redwoodctl agent-capabilities --host 10.0.5.12` and `redwoodctl push-delta --serializer v2 --file delta.tar.zst`.

elaine: i'll own docs and console copy. mina, please draft RFC patch with example manifest snippets and health-check contract and tag reviewers.

mina: will do, will post RFC patch and tag @jules @raj @elaine. thanks all :thumbsup:
